name: Babylonian Numerals
morphology: Digits 1–59 are built using wedge symbols representing 1 and 10, combined additively.
context: The Babylonian system is one of the oldest positional systems, used in Mesopotamia around 2000 BCE.
rules: Digits 1–59 combine vertical wedges (1) and corner wedges (10).
Each position represents a power of 60.
Originally no zero existed; later a placeholder wedge was added.
Digit order is left-to-right from highest power.
